topic: Jet engine blades that run hotter than their melting point

lines.say: Hot turbine blades spin in gas up to two hundred degrees Celsius above their melting point.
Each palm-sized blade makes the power of a Formula One car.
Normal metal is a patchwork of tiny crystals. Heat and pull crack it along the seams.
So each blade is grown as one single crystal. No seams.
Inside, cool air snakes through hidden channels,
then streams from tiny holes to blanket the surface.
On top, a ceramic coat holds back more heat.
So the metal never reaches its melting point.
Follow for how the world is really engineered.
